papers.title: The Hermite-Sylvester criterion for real-rooted polynomials
papers.correspondence: Polynomial coefficient reality is encoded as zero imaginary part. The empty-node case is a Lean extension forced to the zero polynomial by the strict degree bound.

records.hypotheses_and_conclusion:
theorem coeff_im_eq_zero_of_eval_compatible
    (nodes : Finset ℂ) (closed : ∀ z ∈ nodes, conj z ∈ nodes)
    (q : Polynomial ℂ) (degree_lt : q.degree < (nodes.card : WithBot ℕ))
    (compatible : ∀ z ∈ nodes, q.eval (conj z) = conj (q.eval z))
    (n : ℕ) : (q.coeff n).im = 0
records.primary_argument: The finite node set is conjugation-stable, degree is strictly below its cardinality, and evaluations commute with conjugation. Compare the conjugated polynomial with the original on all nodes; bounded-degree uniqueness makes them equal, hence every coefficient is real.
records.limits_and_missing_bridges: Without the degree bound, a polynomial vanishing at every node need not have real coefficients. No nonempty-root or analytic positivity conclusion follows.

papers.title: The Hermite-Sylvester criterion for real-rooted polynomials
papers.locator: Lemma 2 proof, PDF page 2, using Lemma 1
papers.correspondence: The paper uses the particular values i, -i and zero. Lean proves the more general compatible-value interpolation statement and admits empty node sets. Node multiplicities impose no extra interpolation conditions.

records.hypotheses_and_conclusion:
theorem exists_real_interpolate
    (nodes : Finset ℂ) (closed : ∀ z ∈ nodes, conj z ∈ nodes)
    (values : ℂ → ℂ)
    (compatible : ∀ z ∈ nodes, values (conj z) = conj (values z)) :
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℝ, p.degree < (nodes.card : WithBot ℕ) ∧
      ∀ z ∈ nodes, p.eval₂ Complex.ofRealHom z = values z
records.primary_argument: Use Mathlib Lagrange interpolation for conjugation-compatible values on a finite conjugation-stable set, then the preceding coefficient-reality theorem to descend coefficients to real numbers.
records.limits_and_missing_bridges: Without conjugation-compatible data, real interpolation can fail. This generalization is not presented as a verbatim statement of Lemma 2.

papers.title: The Hermite-Sylvester criterion for real-rooted polynomials
papers.locator: Lemma 2 and Theorem 1 necessity proof, PDF pages 2-3
papers.correspondence: Lean uses arbitrary real weights and distinct nodes. The paper later specializes weights to root multiplicities. The signed square has no complex conjugation.

records.hypotheses_and_conclusion:
theorem exists_pair_test {nodes : Finset ℂ}
    (hclosed : ∀ z ∈ nodes, conj z ∈ nodes) (weight : ℂ → ℝ)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ nodes) (him : z.im ≠ 0) :
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℝ, p.degree < (nodes.card : WithBot ℕ) ∧
      squareTrace nodes weight p = -((weight z + weight (conj z) : ℝ) : ℂ)
records.primary_argument: Choose i and -i on a selected nonreal conjugate pair and zero elsewhere. Real interpolation produces a bounded-degree test whose weighted squared evaluations sum to minus the two selected weights.
records.limits_and_missing_bridges: This test needs a selected nonreal node and conjugation closure. It is finite algebra and supplies no positivity theorem for an analytic or arithmetic source.

papers.title: The Hermite-Sylvester criterion for real-rooted polynomials
papers.locator: Theorem 1 and its interpolation proof, PDF pages 2-3
papers.correspondence: This is the finite weighted-node core. It does not construct the paper’s Hermite matrix, identify its quadratic form with the trace, or enumerate roots of a given nonconstant polynomial. Those source-return bridges remain separate.

records.primary_argument: On a finite conjugation-stable set with strictly positive node weights, positivity of all bounded-degree signed-square tests is equivalent to every node being real. A nonreal pair gives a negative test; real nodes give a sum of nonnegative weighted squares.
records.limits_and_missing_bridges: Allowing zero weights can hide nonreal nodes. The degree cutoff and conjugation closure are retained. No RH or unbounded analytic consequence is asserted.

papers.title: Cellular Sheaves of Lattices and the Tarski Laplacian
papers.locator: Section 2.5, cellular incidence restrictions and global sections, equation (5)
papers.correspondence: The implementation uses typed sets and arbitrary local gate relations, not the paper’s lattice-valued category. It is a concrete local-to-global application of the cited incidence convention, not a formalization of the Tarski Laplacian or a proved categorical equivalence.

records.hypotheses_and_conclusion:
theorem uniqueGlue {U : Open C} {family : I → Open C} (cover : Cover U family)
    (patch : (i : I) → Section (family i)) (matchLocal : Compatible patch) :
    ∃! candidate : Section U, ∀ i, candidate.restrict (cover.inside i) = patch i
records.primary_argument: For an incidence-open cover and compatible exact wire assignments satisfying each local gate relation, choose a covering patch for each wire. Compatibility makes the choice independent; a patch covering a gate checks its relation. Wirewise equality proves uniqueness.
records.limits_and_missing_bridges: A cover missing a wire or agreement weakened to a lossy sign observation cannot justify exact unique gluing. No solver termination or polynomial-root existence follows.

papers.title: Cellular Sheaves of Lattices and the Tarski Laplacian
papers.locator: Section 2.5, global-section compatibility equation (5); local path specialization
papers.correspondence: This path-trace result is local work using the cited method, not a named theorem claimed to occur in the paper. No lattice, Hodge or diffusion theorem is imported.

records.hypotheses_and_conclusion:
theorem uniqueTrace {step : Fin (n + 1) → Port → Port → Prop}
    (witness : (g : Fin (n + 1)) → GateWitness step g)
    (matching : Compatible (fun g => (witness g).toSection)) :
    ∃! trace : Trace step,
      ∀ g, trace.toSection.restrict (starCover.inside g) = (witness g).toSection
records.primary_argument: Matching exact gate witnesses on the path star cover glue by uniqueGlue. Convert between a global section and a trace; the inverse conversions transfer the unique-gluing property to traces.
records.mathematical_consumer: Exact verification of a supplied compatible path witness.
records.limits_and_missing_bridges: The result assumes exact matching witnesses. It does not construct witnesses or prove existence of a root or algorithmic termination.
